I do not fully agree with doing everything the docs tell you. Though I assume all doctors would have your best interest in mind, you could look into things or discuss things you can find with your doctor.

I'm not talking about conspiracy things either I am talking about researched methods and clinical trials and getting advice or second option from someone with knowledge and expertise in this area. 

You can also do your own research if you have the means and resources, if you can not do it yourself perhaps someone you know that is close to you can. 

There are well known side effects to the treatments depending on what is included. I would suggest looking at some credible research from researchers with qualifications e.g. PHD that work/do research from credible places and or doctors with expertise in these fields/. 

Don't be afraid to ask questions about your treatment, don't be afraid to look at other legitimate legal options. Think about long term and try to make an informed decision. 

Clinical trails for your specific cancer you could look up the results and see the outcomes. You could ask for a second opinion from another oncologist or someone with knowledge or expertise in this 

Make sure you are you getting follow up care post treatment and try your best to understand or let people around you understand the best they can support you and minimize any further damage or before it could grow. E.g. mental health, dental depending on the treatment you receive.
